newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals seen opening little changed.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals seen opening little changed.

text.p: New York precious metals futures were called to open little changed Monday as the bullion market regained some composure overnight following last week's slide to new three year lows in gold.
But with the dollar remaining near a 47-month high against yen and 31-month high against the mark, the pressure was likely to remain on gold, traders said.
The price of gold in rand terms slide to new nine-month lows in South African rand overnight, prompting more concern about potential South African producer hedging.

Meanwhile, concern about European central bank sales was confirmed when the European Union's statistics body, Eurostat, affirmed an earlier understanding that central bank gold sales could be used to reduce debt-to-GDP ratios to help meet the EMU criteria, but not be used to improve fiscal ratios.
COMEX April gold was called unchanged to up $0.50 from Friday's close of $346.00 an ounce. It traded from $345.90 to $346.80 on ACCESS.
In the bullion market, spot gold was quoted at $344.10/60 early. It fixed at a fresh three-year low of $343.75 in London this morning.
COMEX gold stocks were unchanged Thursday at 816,755 ounces.
COMEX March silver was called unchanged to down 2.0 cents from Friday's close of $4.920. It traded from $4.920 to $4.875 on ACCESS.
COMEX silver stocks rose 661,650 ounces Friday to 194,849,459 ounces.
NYMEX April platinum was called unchanged to $0.50 lower from the previous close at $353.00.
NYMEX March palladium was called little changed from Friday's close of $125.65 after it caught up with Friday's COMEX move and fixed at its highest level since last September at $124.30 in London.
